files.lang.knl:
(* Kanon's built-in bool module, which [use builtin "bool"] reads: here
   bool.knl and bool.kn are copies of it, which [use "bool"] uses, to read and
   to edit. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "bool"
files.bool.knl:
(* The bool module, at the bottom of every language: booleans, equality, [Ite]
   and [Distinct]. See the README of Kanon for the syntax. *)

node Bool of bool : TBool
notation Bool
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem]
node Or : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem]
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]
node Ite : TBool -> a -> a -> a
node Distinct : a list -> TBool
sort TBool

infix "&&" = And, and_
infix "||" = Or, or_
infix "==" = Eq, eq
prefix "not" = Not, not_

constant true = v_true
constant false = v_false
files.bool.kn:
(* The bool module, at the bottom of every language: booleans, equality, [Ite]
   and [Distinct]. The modules above it add their rules to its rule functions
   with [extend rule], and their literals to [sure_neq] with [extend fn].

   Primitives are implemented by hand by each language, in OCaml and in Lean.
   Oracles have no Lean definition: the Lean model is parameterised by them,
   and the properties that the proofs rely on are stated with the language.
   Here, they are the hash-consing order. *)

(* {1 Primitives} *)

(* Sorts terms along the hash-consing order. *)
oracle sort_by_tag : t list -> t list

prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

(* {1 Helpers} *)

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false

(* whether [a] and [b] surely have different values: the modules above add
   their literals *)
fn sure_neq (a b : t) : bool =
  (not (type_of a = type_of b))
  ||
  match (a, b) with
  | Bool a, Bool b -> not (a = b)
  | _ -> false

fn at_most_one (l : t list) : bool =
  match l with [] | [ _ ] -> true | _ -> false

(* {1 Rules} *)

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | false_: false && _ -> v_false
  | true_: true && x -> x
  | not: p && not p -> v_false
  | and_: (a && _ as x) && a -> x
  | or_: (a || _) && a -> a
  | eq_neq: a == x && a == y when sure_neq x y -> v_false

rule or_ : Or (v1, v2) =
  | true_: true || _ -> v_true
  | false_: false || x -> x
  | not: p || not p -> v_true
  | or_: (a || _ as x) || a -> x
  | and_: (a && _) || a -> a

rule not_ : Not sv =
  | true_: true -> v_false
  | false_: false -> v_true
  | not: not sv -> sv
  | or_: v1 || v2 -> not v1 && not v2
  | and_: v1 && v2 -> not v1 || not v2
  | ite: Ite (g, a, b) -> ite g (not a) (not b)
  | distinct: Distinct [ l; r ] -> l == r

rule ite : Ite (guard, if_, else_) =
  | true_: true, _, _ -> if_
  | false_: false, _, _ -> else_
  | bool: _, true, false -> guard
  | not_bool: _, false, true -> not guard
  | false_then: _, false, _ -> not guard && else_
  | true_then: _, true, _ -> guard || else_
  | false_else: _, _, false -> guard && if_
  | true_else: _, _, true -> not guard || if_
  | not_guard: not g, _, _ -> ite g else_ if_
  | guard_then: g, g, _ -> guard || else_
  | guard_else: g, _, g -> guard && if_
  | ite_then: g, Ite (g, x, _), _ -> ite guard x else_
  | ite_else: g, _, Ite (g, _, y) -> ite guard if_ y
  | and_ite_then: g && _, Ite (g, x, _), _ -> ite guard x else_
  | or_ite_else: g || _, _, Ite (g, _, y) -> ite guard if_ y
  | same: _, x, x -> if_

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: v == v -> v_true
  | bools: Bool b1 == Bool b2 -> of_bool (b1 = b2)
  (* distributing over a shared guard lets the branches cancel pairwise *)
  | ite_ite: Ite (b, l, r) == Ite (b, l', r') -> ite b (l == l') (r == r')
  | false_: false == x -> not x
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | nots: not b == not c -> b == c

(* The equality of terms that may have different sorts, false when they do:
   [@untyped], so its operands are not asserted to have the same sort. *)
rule eq_untyped : Eq (v1, v2) [@untyped] =
  | ill_typed: _ when not (type_of v1 = type_of v2) -> v_false
  | typed: _ -> v1 == v2

(* [distinct_check_one a rest] and [distinct_check l] go through the pairs of
   elements in order, and stop at the first pair that is equal ([Some false])
   or not surely different ([None]). *)
fn distinct_check_one (a : t) (rest : t list) : bool option =
  match rest with
  | [] -> Some true
  | b :: rest ->
      if a = b then Some false
      else if sure_neq a b then distinct_check_one a rest
      else None

fn distinct_check (l : t list) : bool option =
  match l with
  | [] -> Some true
  | a :: rest -> (
      match distinct_check_one a rest with
      | Some true -> distinct_check rest
      | r -> r)

rule distinct : Distinct l =
  | small: _ when at_most_one l -> v_true
  | distinct: _ when distinct_check l = Some true -> v_true
  | not_distinct: _ when distinct_check l = Some false -> v_false
  | default: _ -> Distinct (sort_by_tag l)

let node : kind -> ty -> t =
  let module H = Ephemeron.K1.Make (struct
    type nonrec t = t
    let equal a b = equal_kind a.kind b.kind && equal_ty a.ty b.ty
    let hash a = hash_combine (hash_kind a.kind) (hash_ty a.ty)
  end) in
  let table = H.create 1024 and tags = ref 0 in
  fun kind ty ->
    let v = { kind; ty; tag = -1 } in
    match H.find table v with
    | t -> t
    | exception Not_found ->
      let t = { v with tag = !tags } in
      incr tags;
      H.add table t t;
      t

theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) :
  ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { orc := h,
      bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Refinement.refl,
      bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Refinement.refl,
      bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_distinct := fun l => Refinement.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { orc := hO.orc,
      bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_ite := Bool.ite.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq := Bool.eq.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step_sound _ hO }

(* An example language made of Kanon's bool module alone (modules/bool.kn[l],
   built into kanon, use builtin "bool"), and of variables: Kanon generates the types of
   its terms from these nodes. Its Lean model is in lean/; [kanon ocaml-types]
   and [kanon ocaml] generate its OCaml types and rules, with the primitives of
   the module [Prims]. *)

[@@@lean_root "BoolExample"]
[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use builtin "bool"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "Int"] [@noeq]

node Var of var

[@@@warning "-a"]

type var = string

and kind =
  | Var of var
  | Bool of bool
  | Op1 of op1 * t
  | Op2 of op2 * t * t
  | Op3 of op3 * t * t * t
  | OpN of opn * (t list)

and op1 =
  | Not

and op2 =
  | And
  | Or
  | Eq

and op3 =
  | Ite

and opn =
  | Distinct

and ty =
  | TBool

and t = {
  kind : kind;
  ty : ty;
  tag : int;
}

let hash_combine x y = (x * 65599) + y

let rec equal_t (a : t) (b : t) = Int.equal a.tag b.tag

and hash_t (a : t) = a.tag

and equal_var (a : var) (b : var) = Stdlib.( = ) a b

and hash_var (a : var) = Hashtbl.hash a

and equal_kind (a : kind) (b : kind) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Var a1, Var b1 -> equal_var a1 b1
  | Bool a1, Bool b1 -> Stdlib.Bool.equal a1 b1
  | Op1 (a1, a2), Op1 (b1, b2) -> equal_op1 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2
  | Op2 (a1, a2, a3), Op2 (b1, b2, b3) ->
      equal_op2 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2 && equal_t a3 b3
  | Op3 (a1, a2, a3, a4), Op3 (b1, b2, b3, b4) ->
      equal_op3 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2 && equal_t a3 b3 && equal_t a4 b4
  | OpN (a1, a2), OpN (b1, b2) ->
      equal_opn a1 b1 && (Stdlib.List.equal equal_t) a2 b2
  | _ -> false

and hash_kind (a : kind) =
  match a with
  | Var a1 -> hash_combine (0) (hash_var a1)
  | Bool a1 -> hash_combine (1) (Stdlib.Bool.to_int a1)
  | Op1 (a1, a2) -> hash_combine (hash_combine (2) (hash_op1 a1)) (hash_t a2)
  | Op2 (a1, a2, a3) ->
      hash_combine
        (hash_combine (hash_combine (3) (hash_op2 a1)) (hash_t a2))
        (hash_t a3)
  | Op3 (a1, a2, a3, a4) ->
      hash_combine
        (hash_combine
           (hash_combine (hash_combine (4) (hash_op3 a1)) (hash_t a2))
           (hash_t a3)) (hash_t a4)
  | OpN (a1, a2) ->
      hash_combine (hash_combine (5) (hash_opn a1))
        ((Stdlib.List.fold_left (fun acc x -> hash_combine acc (hash_t x)) 0) a2)

and equal_op1 (a : op1) (b : op1) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Not, Not -> true

and hash_op1 (a : op1) =
  match a with
  | Not -> 0

and equal_op2 (a : op2) (b : op2) =
  match (a, b) with
  | And, And -> true
  | Or, Or -> true
  | Eq, Eq -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_op2 (a : op2) =
  match a with
  | And -> 0
  | Or -> 1
  | Eq -> 2

and equal_op3 (a : op3) (b : op3) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Ite, Ite -> true

and hash_op3 (a : op3) =
  match a with
  | Ite -> 0

and equal_opn (a : opn) (b : opn) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Distinct, Distinct -> true

and hash_opn (a : opn) =
  match a with
  | Distinct -> 0

and equal_ty (a : ty) (b : ty) =
  match (a, b) with
  | TBool, TBool -> true

and hash_ty (a : ty) =
  match a with
  | TBool -> 0

(* Not safe across domains (TODO). *)
let node : kind -> ty -> t =
  let module H = Ephemeron.K1.Make (struct
    type nonrec t = t
    let equal a b = equal_kind a.kind b.kind && equal_ty a.ty b.ty
    let hash a = hash_combine (hash_kind a.kind) (hash_ty a.ty)
  end) in
  let table = H.create 1024 and tags = ref 0 in
  fun kind ty ->
    let v = { kind; ty; tag = -1 } in
    match H.find table v with
    | t -> t
    | exception Not_found ->
      let t = { v with tag = !tags } in
      incr tags;
      H.add table t t;
      t

(* An example language of integers and of arrays of integers: it shows the
   built-in immutable arrays, whose type [int array] is the argument of a node,

   and its Lean model is in lean/. *)

(* The vec module: integers, and arrays of integers. *)

node Int of int : TInt
notation Int
node Vec of int array : TVec

(** The number of elements of an array. *)
node Len : TVec -> TInt

(** The element at an index, which must be in bounds. *)
node Get : TVec -> TInt -> TInt

(** The array with the element at an index replaced: a copy. *)
node Set : TVec -> TInt -> TInt -> TVec

sort TInt
sort TVec
files.vec.kn:
(* The rules of the vec module. *)

fn in_bounds (a : int array) (i : int) : bool = 0 <= i && i < array_length a

rule len : Len v =
  | lit: Vec a -> Int (array_length a)

rule get : Get (v, i) =
  | lit: Vec a, #k when in_bounds a k -> Int (array_get a k)
  | set_same: Set (_, j, x), k when j = k -> x

rule set : Set (v, i, x) =
  | lit: Vec a, #k, #y when in_bounds a k -> Vec (array_set a k y)

(* arrays are compared structurally *)
fn same (a b : int array) : bool = a = b

(* the conversions between lists and arrays *)
fn of_list (l : int list) : t = Vec (array_of_list l)

fn elements (v : t) : int list =
  match v with
  | Vec a -> array_to_list a
  | _ -> []

    vec_len := Vec.len.step O,
    vec_get := Vec.get.step O,

(* A small value language: booleans and mathematical integers, in one module.
   Kanon generates the types of its terms from its nodes: its OCaml types are
   those of [kanon ocaml-types], in the module [Tiny_types], and its
   primitives are in the module [Tiny_prims]. Its rules are in rules.kn. *)

[@@@ocaml_types "Tiny_types"]
[@@@ocaml_prims "Tiny_prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Tiny_rules"]

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"] [@noeq] [@equal "String.equal"]
  [@hash "Hashtbl.hash"]

(* types of the module Tiny_base, which ocaml-types re-exports *)
type checked [@ocaml "Tiny_base.checked"] = { signed : bool; unsigned : bool }
type rounding [@ocaml "Tiny_base.rounding"] = Nearest | Zero

node Var of var
node Bool of bool
node Int of int : TInt
notation Bool
notation Int
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@fold Rules.add] [@unit 0]
node Times : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 1] [@zero 0]
node Lt : TInt -> TInt -> TBool [@fold Rules.lt]
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]
sort TBool
sort TInt

infix "&&" = And, Rules.and_
infix "+" = Plus, Rules.plus
infix "*" = Times, Rules.times
infix "<" = Lt, Rules.lt_
infix "==" = Eq, Rules.eq
prefix "not" = Not, Rules.not_

constant false = Rules.v_false

prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y
fn lt (x y : int) : bool = x < y

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2)
rule times : Times (v1, v2)
rule lt_ : Lt (v1, v2)

rule not_ : Not v =
  | lit: true -> v_false
  | not_not: not x -> x

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> v_false

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> v_true
  | lits: Int x == Int y -> of_bool (x = y)

(* a parameter of a sort, asserted on entry *)
fn is_zero (v : TInt) : bool =
  match v with
  | 0 -> true
  | _ -> false

(* a node built at a sort *)
fn zero : t = (Int 0 : TInt)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) :
  ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { orc := h,
      bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Refinement.refl,
      bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Refinement.refl,
      bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_distinct := fun l => Refinement.refl,
      rules_xor := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { orc := hO.orc,
      bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_ite := Bool.ite.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq := Bool.eq.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_xor := Rules.xor.step_sound _ hO }

(* A tiny value language: booleans and integers. *)

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"]

(** A variable. *)
node Var of var
(** A boolean literal. *)
node Bool of bool : TBool
(** An integer literal. *)
node Int of int : TInt
(** Negation. *)
node Not : TBool -> TBool
(** Conjunction. *)
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool
(** The sum of two integers. *)
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt
(** Equality of two terms of any sort. *)
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool

(** The sort of booleans. *)
sort TBool
(** The sort of integers. *)
sort TInt

notation Bool
notation Int

  | Int of Z.t (** An integer literal. *)

  | Op2 of op2 * t * t

and op1 =
  | Not (** Negation. *)

and op2 =
  | And (** Conjunction. *)
  | Plus (** The sum of two integers. *)
  | Eq (** Equality of two terms of any sort. *)

and ty =

  | TInt (** The sort of integers. *)

  ty : ty;

let hash_combine x y = (x * 65599) + y

let rec equal_t (a : t) (b : t) = Int.equal a.tag b.tag

and hash_t (a : t) = a.tag

and equal_var (a : var) (b : var) = Stdlib.( = ) a b

and hash_var (a : var) = Hashtbl.hash a

and equal_kind (a : kind) (b : kind) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Var a1, Var b1 -> equal_var a1 b1
  | Bool a1, Bool b1 -> Stdlib.Bool.equal a1 b1
  | Int a1, Int b1 -> Z.equal a1 b1
  | Op1 (a1, a2), Op1 (b1, b2) -> equal_op1 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2
  | Op2 (a1, a2, a3), Op2 (b1, b2, b3) ->
      equal_op2 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2 && equal_t a3 b3
  | _ -> false

and hash_kind (a : kind) =
  match a with
  | Var a1 -> hash_combine (0) (hash_var a1)

(* A tiny value language: booleans and integers. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"]

(** A variable. *)
node Var of var
(** A boolean literal. *)
node Bool of bool : TBool
(** An integer literal. *)
node Int of int : TInt
(** Negation. *)
node Not : TBool -> TBool [@invol] [@fold Rules.negb]
(** Conjunction. *)
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
(** The sum of two integers. *)
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 0] [@fold Rules.add]
(** Equality of two terms of any sort. *)
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]

(** The sort of booleans. *)
sort TBool
(** The sort of integers. *)
sort TInt

notation Bool
notation Int

infix "&&" = And, Rules.and_
infix "+" = Plus, Rules.plus
infix "==" = Eq, Rules.eq
prefix "not" = Not, Rules.not_
files.rules.kn:
(** Whether a variable is surely a natural number. *)
prim var_is_nat : var -> bool

(* Helpers *)
fn negb (b : bool) : bool = not b
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y

(** Whether a term is surely a natural number. *)
fn is_nat (v : t) : bool =
  match v with
  | Int n -> n >= 0
  | Var x -> var_is_nat x
  | l + r -> is_nat l && is_nat r
  | _ -> false

(** A size estimate, for the OCaml code around the simplifier: not modelled in Lean. *)
fn cost (v : t) : int [@no_lean] =
  match v with
  | l + r -> cost l + cost r + 1
  | _ -> 1

(* Rule functions: the rules derived from the laws of their spec come first,
   then these. *)

rule not_ : Not v

(** Conjunction. *)
rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> Bool false

(** Sum: adjacent literals are added. *)
rule plus : Plus (v1, v2) =
  | assoc: (x + #a) + #b -> x + Int (a + b)

(** Equality: literals are compared, and a negative literal differs from a natural number. *)
rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> Bool true
  | lits: Int x == Int y -> Bool (x = y)
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | neg: Int x == y when x < 0 && is_nat y -> Bool false

  | lits: #x lt #y -> Bool.of_bool (x < y)
  | same: x lt x -> Bool.v_false

  | ints: Int x == Int y -> Bool.of_bool (x = y)

extend fn Bool.sure_neq =
  | Int x, Int y -> not (x = y)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) :
  ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { orc := h,
      bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Refinement.refl,
      bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Refinement.refl,
      bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      bool_distinct := fun l => Refinement.refl,
      int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      int_int_lt := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { orc := hO.orc,
      bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_ite := Bool.ite.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq := Bool.eq.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step_sound _ hO,
      int_plus := Int.plus.step_sound _ hO,
      int_int_lt := Int.int_lt.step_sound _ hO }

  type tint = [ `TInt | tnonzero ]

(** The typed interface of the language, organised like it: a module per Kanon module (per file). A term of type [_ t] has a phantom parameter, one of the tags of [Tag], that says what Kanon knows of the term, and the smart constructors check it at compile time. The tag is not data: a term is the same value as its untyped term, [raw]. *)
module type S = sig
  (** The terms and sorts of the types of the language, without tag. *)
  type raw = t
  type raw_ty = ty
  
  (** A term, whose phantom parameter is its tag. *)
  type +'a t
  
  (** A sort of terms of the tag [ 'a ]. *)
  type +'a ty
  
  (** Forgets the tag of a term: the same value. *)
  val untyped : 'a t -> raw
  
  (** Trusts the tag of a term: unchecked. *)
  val type_ : raw -> 'a t
  
  (** Changes the tag of a term: unchecked. *)
  val cast : 'a t -> 'b t
  
  (** Forgets the tag of a sort. *)
  val untype_type : 'a ty -> raw_ty
  
  (** Trusts the tag of a sort: unchecked. *)
  val type_type : raw_ty -> 'a ty
  
  (** The Kanon module int. *)
  module Int : sig
    (** The sort of integers. *)
    val t_int : [> Tag.tint ] ty
    
    (** The sum of two integers. *)
    val plus : [< Tag.tint ] t -> [< Tag.tint ] t -> [> Tag.tint ] t
    
    (** The quotient: the divisor is known to be non-zero. *)
    val div : [< Tag.tint ] t -> [< Tag.tnonzero ] t -> [> Tag.tint ] t
    
    (** The square of an integer plus one, which is not zero. *)
    val sq1 : [< Tag.tint ] t -> [> Tag.tnonzero ] t
    
    val as_int : _ t -> Z.t option
    val is_int : _ t -> bool
    val as_plus : _ t -> ([> Tag.tint ] t * [> Tag.tint ] t) option
    val is_plus : _ t -> bool
    val as_div : _ t -> ([> Tag.tint ] t * [> Tag.tnonzero ] t) option
    val is_div : _ t -> bool
    val as_sq1 : _ t -> [> Tag.tint ] t option
    val is_sq1 : _ t -> bool
    val as_tint : _ ty -> unit option
    val is_tint : _ ty -> bool
  end
end

(** The implementation of [S]: the rules, with the types of [S] visible, [type 'a t = raw]. [S] hides it, since a visible equality would make every tag the same type. It has no constructor for the leaf nodes, which no rule builds: a program adds them around it, with [type_], in [module Typed = struct include (Derived : S) ... end]. *)
module Derived = struct
  include Rules
  
  type raw = t
  type raw_ty = ty
  type nonrec 'a t = raw
  type nonrec 'a ty = raw_ty
  
  let[@inline] untyped (x : 'a t) : raw = x
  let[@inline] type_ (x : raw) : 'a t = x
  let[@inline] cast (x : 'a t) : 'b t = x
  let[@inline] untype_type (x : 'a ty) : raw_ty = x
  let[@inline] type_type (x : raw_ty) : 'a ty = x
end

(** Checks that the rules satisfy [S], whatever their tags. *)
module _ : S = Derived

  int_div : Term → Term → Term

  (Term.mk (Kind.Op2 Op2.Div v1 v2) Ty.TInt)

@[kanon_spec] def Int.sq1.spec (v : Term) : Term :=
  (Term.mk (Kind.Op1 Op1.Sq1 v) Ty.TInt)

    | _, _ => none)

    | x, (Term.mk (Kind.Int kanon__2) _) =>

    | _, _ => none)
  <|> (match v1, v2 with

        (whenSome (decide (kanon__2 = (0 : Int))) (x))
        | _, _ => none)

    | _, _ =>
    (whenSome true ((Term.mk (mk_commut_binop O Op2.Plus v1 v2) Ty.TInt))))

  (firstSome [Int.plus.r_lits O v1 v2, Int.plus.r_unit_zero O v1 v2, Int.plus.r_default O v1 v2]).getD (Int.plus.spec v1 v2)

def Int.div.r_self (O : Ops) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) : Option Term :=
  (match v1, v2 with
    | x, y =>
    (whenSome (decide (x = y)) ((Term.mk (Kind.Int (1 : Int)) Ty.TInt))))

def Int.div.r_default (O : Ops) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) : Option Term :=
  (match v1, v2 with
    | _, _ =>
    (whenSome true ((Term.mk (Kind.Op2 Op2.Div v1 v2) Ty.TInt))))

  { orc := orc,
    int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Int.plus.spec v1 v2,
    int_div := fun v1 v2 => Int.div.spec v1 v2,
    int_sq1 := fun v => Int.sq1.spec v }

def opsStep (O : Ops) : Ops :=
  { orc := O.orc,
    int_plus := Int.plus.step O,
    int_div := Int.div.step O,
    int_sq1 := Int.sq1.step O }

  match a with

        (hash_t a3)

and equal_op2 (a : op2) (b : op2) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Plus, Plus -> true
  | Div, Div -> true
  | Lt, Lt -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_op2 (a : op2) =
  match a with
  | Plus -> 0
  | Div -> 1
  | Lt -> 2

and equal_ty (a : ty) (b : ty) =
  match (a, b) with
  | TInt, TInt -> true
  | TBool, TBool -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_ty (a : ty) =
  match a with
  | TInt -> 0
  | TBool -> 1

(* Not safe across domains (TODO). *)
let node : kind -> ty -> t =
  let module H = Ephemeron.K1.Make (struct
    type nonrec t = t
    let equal a b = equal_kind a.kind b.kind && equal_ty a.ty b.ty
    let hash a = hash_combine (hash_kind a.kind) (hash_ty a.ty)
  end) in
  let table = H.create 1024 and tags = ref 0 in
  fun kind ty ->
    let v = { kind; ty; tag = -1 } in
    match H.find table v with
    | t -> t
    | exception Not_found ->
      let t = { v with tag = !tags } in
      incr tags;
      H.add table t t;
      t

        | _, _ => none)

    int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Int.plus.spec v1 v2,
    int_div := fun v1 v2 => Int.div.spec v1 v2,

    int_div := Int.div.step O,
    int_int_lt := Int.int_lt.step O }
